# REPLAY150_R1 replay snapshot test

Staged: `DriverSF_V29s_160Capacity_150Request_REPLAY150_R1.asi`.
Release/Win32, 234496 bytes, SHA256
`2ab7f763f216abfaf5091308f0adb3e428512038d2f0384432faa140aae12dd9`.

This includes PARKED150_R1 and the validated streaming/audio/cleanup parents.
It corrects the full traffic snapshot's overlapping 50-entry layout, with
150 traffic IDs and 256 retained-reference records in separate storage.
The actual retained-vehicle game pool is unchanged. Requests150, graphics160,
ED/EF sidecars, parked weights/population and refresh timing are unchanged.
It is fixture-verified and staged, not installed or game-tested by the agent.

## Setup

Use exactly one traffic ASI in the game's loader directory: this one instead
of PARKED150_R1 or another traffic test. Keep the same adjusted
`san_franciscoAI.fchunk` used for the successful parked test, to isolate this
change. No AI asset is included or modified by this build.

Start a fresh game process and make a fresh recording in this session.
Existing recordings that already contain model0 in place of a real vehicle
cannot be reconstructed automatically. The native record format is preserved;
valid older recordings are supported within the150/256 snapshot capacities.

## Sequence

1. Enter Story and drive for about1–2 minutes. Check moving/parked variety and
   engine/tire/horn audio.
2. Enter Replay, leave it, return to Story and drive briefly.
3. Enter Replay again, then leave it. Repeat this Story/Replay cycle at least
   three times; this is the previously problematic order.
4. Return to the main menu, reload Story, try a Challenge, and repeat a Replay
   entry/exit if available. Finish by quitting normally.

Note any loading stall/crash, approximate step where it occurred, parked-car
regression, rendering/audio issue, or substantial FPS change.

## Log and interpretation

The log is `%TEMP%\DSFV29s_replay150_<PID>.log`. Copy it to `dist/MAIN_150`.
If the game stalls, keep the same log and provide a Task Manager dump as before.

Require `DSFV29s_REPLAY150_START revision=1 status=1 hooks=7` as well as the
inherited successful startup markers. Snapshot `capture`, `save`, `import`
and `restore` events show counts and roster hashes. The canonical150 roster
should retain `id50=181 has181=1` with the same hash across boundaries.
An ordinary native18-car roster need not contain181; that alone is not a fault.

STATUS records include snapshot phase, replay loading/lifecycle state, clock,
event cursor, simulation-manager pointer and pending traffic/reference counts.
They describe sampled state and do not independently prove a softlock.
`invalid=0`, no replay FATAL, and balanced completed temporary work are expected.
`activeTemps` can be nonzero during a sampled operation; a single sample is not
a leak. Bad signatures/bounds/cache guards fail explicitly with
`DSFV29s_REPLAY150_FATAL` and exit code`0x29F4`; there is no silent recovery exit.

This correction does not bypass the separate null simulation-manager pause
crash. It also does not yet establish that snapshot corruption was the sole
cause of the supplied loading softlock. The live sequence above is needed.

Analysis after the run:

```powershell
python -B scripts/analyze_baseline150_log.py dist/MAIN_150/DSFV29s_replay150_<PID>.log --output analysis/replay150_<PID>_baseline.json
python -B scripts/analyze_callback_log.py dist/MAIN_150/DSFV29s_replay150_<PID>.log --output analysis/replay150_<PID>_callback.json
```
